shargaotis:study:1.title: Bustards (Aves: Otididae) from the Middle Miocene of Mongolia (Paleontological Journal, 2025)

facts.statement: Shargaotis is an extinct genus of bird belonging to the family Otididae, commonly known as bustards.
facts.quote: Shargaotis () is an extinct genus of bird in the family Otididae (bustards)

facts.statement: Shargaotis lived during the Middle Miocene epoch in Mongolia.
facts.quote: known the Middle Miocene of Mongolia

facts.statement: The genus Shargaotis contains only one known species, Shargaotis ignipes, which is known from a fragment of a tibiotarsus.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Shargaotis ignipes, known from a fragment of a tibiotarsus

facts.statement: Shargaotis is most similar to the living genera Otis and Chlamydotis.
facts.quote: Shargaotis is most similar to the extant genera Otis and Chlamydotis

facts.statement: Shargaotis fossils were discovered at the Sharga locality in western Mongolia, which contains Miocene-aged rock outcrops.
facts.quote: The Shargaotis fossil material was discovered at the 'Sharga locality', representing Miocene-dated outcrops in western Mongolia

facts.statement: The fossils were collected during Soviet/Russian-Mongolian Paleontological Expeditions conducted in 1978, 1979, 1984, and 2001.
facts.quote: It was collected as part of the Soviet / Russian–Mongolian Paleontological Expeditions, which were conducted in 1978, 1979, 1984, and 2001

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is housed at the Paleontological Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences under accession number PIN 4869/249.
facts.quote: The specimen is housed at the Paleontological Institute, part of the Russian Academy of Sciences, where it is permanently accessioned as specimen PIN, no. 4869/249

facts.statement: The genus name Shargaotis combines the type locality 'Sharga' with the name of the great bustard, Otis.
facts.quote: The generic name, Shargaotis, combines a reference to the type locality (Sharga) with Otis, the generic name of the closely related extant great bustard (Otis tarda)

facts.statement: The species name ignipes means 'fiery-footed' or 'extremely fast' in Latin.
facts.quote: The specific name, ignipes, is derived from Latin roots meaning fiery-footed, and by extension, extremely fast

facts.statement: Three other bustard bone fragments from the Sharga locality are known, including a distal left tibiotarsus (PIN 4869/250) that is distinct from Shargaotis.
facts.quote: Three additional isolated bustard bone fragments are known from the Sharga locality, including PIN, no. 4869/250, a distal left tibiotarsus distinct from that of Shargaotis

facts.statement: A base phalanx forming the major wing finger (PIN 4869/235) is known from the locality.
facts.quote: The third specimen, PIN, no. 4869/235, is the base phalanx forming the major wing finger

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that two additional bustard fragments similar to Chlamydotis might belong to Shargaotis, though they are currently classified as indeterminate.
facts.quote: However, the similarity of the latter two to Chlamydotis suggests they may be referrable to this taxon

facts.statement: Shargaotis lived during the Miocene epoch.
The description of Shargaotis was published online in 2026, with an issue date of December 2025.
facts.quote: Published online in 2026, but the issue date is listed as December 2025
